phase: Phase 3: reviewed Total barriers, French/Pilchuck Creek corrections and mapped current tidal influence
tidal_source_notes: Landscape connectivity, not feature connectivity, controls selection; disconnected/developed/unknown classes are excluded.
Partially and significantly restricted tidal polygons remain tidally influenced and are included.

Layer 2 maps large river deltas (primarily circa 2020); layer 3 extends mapping along remaining Puget Sound nearshore (review completed 2024; report 2025). Original per-feature dates and certainty fields are retained.
PMEP base mapping explicitly includes the freshwater tidal zone but also historical disconnected areas; the CFS current connectivity classifications distinguish those areas.
The draft 2022 PMEP basis is modeled maximum tidal flooding under current topography and extreme tidal water levels; it is not a universal daily-high-tide contour.

Published geometry is NAD83(HARN) Washington South State Plane US survey feet (EPSG:2927); cached analysis geometry is EPSG:26910. The polygons publish no vertical coordinate/datum cutoff, so no NAVD88 or MHHW elevation is inferred.
This is a mapped current tidal-influence proxy; it is not an exact surveyed, discharge-independent top-of-tide line, floodplain boundary, future sea-level-rise scenario, or salinity boundary.

Source polygons can contain channel gaps or classification seams; direct spatial clipping requires an independent channel coverage check. No whole stream component may be deleted solely because it connects to tidal water.
Source overlap is measured before union; areas where one source is selected and the other unselected are deferred from the cut mask rather than overriding uncertain/non-tidal data.
Published source records with empty native and GeoJSON geometry are retained as explicit holds, never fabricated: CFS2025:3:3818

Substantive invalid-source repairs (area change over 1 m2) are retained for review but held from the cut mask: CFS2025:3:232, CFS2025:3:741, CFS2025:3:862, CFS2025:3:872, CFS2025:3:1074, CFS2025:3:1300, CFS2025:3:1961, CFS2025:3:1991, CFS2025:3:3997, CFS2025:3:4478, CFS2025:3:5118, CFS2025:3:5541
NWI R1 is specifically freshwater riverine tidal habitat; it extends to the upstream limit of tidal fluctuations in the FWS classification.
The public NWI service is refreshed biannually, but source imagery/project dates vary and are retained in source_vintage_join. Service retrieval date is not the imagery date.
Any overlap with CFS current Completely Restricted, Developed, or Unknown classes is held rather than allowing older NWI mapping to override current evidence.
NWI is biological wetland/deepwater mapping with scale and interpretation limitations, not a flow-dependent surveyed head-of-tide boundary; narrower channels and classification seams can be omitted.
CFS base cache and all existing scenario products are unchanged by this comparison/supplement preparation.
The returned polygons and mask contain only approved NWI additions outside the frozen CFS current-tidal mask; union with CFS once, rather than adding overlapping miles.
NWI additions are screened against current CFS complete non-tidal, developed, unknown, and held malformed-source footprints; conflict geometry and class-resolved audits are explicit.
Neither mapped dataset reaches every published weak, discharge-dependent tidal backwater limit. No extra polygon or cutoff is invented across this remaining evidence gap.
The gap geometry records deferred mapped NWI conflicts only; it does not purport to bound all unmapped physical tidal influence.
